name: Pocket Timeline, Traced
tagline: A pocket instrument on slate: one steel line of time down every page, lit only where something is live, and the next four weeks drawn in light on the tube.
concept: Every page hangs from one 1px steel line of time. The line leaves the page's title tile (on Home, the lit NOW plate) and plugs each section in at an 8px square node. A node lights only while its section holds something live, and past LATER or SOMEDAY the line runs on dotted for a short stretch and stops. The glass carries time too: Next up traces the next four weeks as square pulses, the month tube draws the same pulse rising from each week's baseline, To do is a due queue cut by a lit NOW line, and Chat is a two-sided axis that ends in the lit box, with NOW as the box's tab. The feel is a calm slate handheld where every line means time or order. The original phosphor light (bloom, blur, scanlines, halos, breathing lamps) sits only on the glass and on what is live.
companions: Grounded companions do the work, and each has one job. Slate is for what the family owns: #12171a trays, #161c20 cartridges, and #1f272d for the 'here' cell and latched keys. Steel is for structure: #4b5963 for the line, #707e88 for hollow nodes, #a9b6bf for labels. Bone (#dcd8cb) is for titles and heads. Denim (#9db6d6) is for every link and for the family's bubble edge. Amber (#eaa85d) means late or needs a look: late ticks and the late node, 'was due' words, the setup edge and its square step numbers, and the Status panels that need attention (their node, turn-in, rule, icon and edge). It also appears in the family's initial rings in Chat. It no longer fills the restaurants row, which is now a slate cartridge with the restaurant kind colour only in its icon's ring. Each part of the site keeps its colour only as marks: its title tile, its trail, its turn-in and run-on rule, and its 2px cap in the bar. Coming up and Plans are pale ice cyan #98dcef, To do lemon, Ideas lilac, wishes pink, and Status, Settings and Chat sage #86d9a6. The cartridges' 3px kind caps use the kind colours. The #6dff9c phosphor is kept to a short list: the mark and cursor, Send and the other single primaries, 'next', the two lit boxes (Home and Chat), focus, the NOW and NEXT plates, live nodes, lamps, the trace and pulses, and the tubes.
decisions: Kept the lineage fixes as the brief gives them. Palette: green-black #0a0e0c, slate surfaces, bone heads, denim accent, graphite bezel, lit #86d9a6, and brand, halo and screen #6dff9c at glow 0.95 and screenGlow 1.0. Single 1px #2b3338 frames with a 2px radius. The Lucide sprite. Words for every place. 44px on every target (0 small targets on all 13 renders).

A written type scale that holds on every page. The Home question is Instrument Sans 600 at clamp(2rem, 3.6vw, 2.625rem). Page titles are 2.5rem, section heads ('Coming up', 'September 2026', '12 ideas') 1.5rem, and panel and shelf heads 1.25rem, all at wdth 84-86 in bone. Page row titles are Plex 600 17px, and shelf rows ('Call the dentist…', cartridge titles, the restaurants row, kids' names) drop to 16px. Figures are Plex Mono 500 at 14px, tabular. VT323 appears only on glass. A head never ranks below the rows it governs.

Feature 1, Grid Console's lit spine, now follows the law without exceptions. A node is a summary lamp. It lights green only for what is live: NOW, the breathing NEXT, Coming up while a plan is today, this month's head, the current settings page, Status's Who answers while a model answers, and the spend tube. It goes amber for late or needs a look, and stays hollow steel otherwise. Every panel on the line now has a run-on head rule after its words, the way Coming up does. The turn-in moved onto the panel's own ::before (centred on the head's 24px line), which frees the h2's ::after for the rule.

Feature 2, Bench Scope's four-week trace, is kept whole on Home: the lit trigger, flat square pulses whose height counts plans, the intensified and pinging next pulse, VT323 day numbers matching the Coming up leaves, 'Oct' at the month turn, and 'NEXT 4 WEEKS · 1 WK/DIV' on the trim. On a narrow glass the radar steps down to 4.25rem so 'Silver Falls hike' holds one line. There the trace labels only the next pulse and the start of each week, and a week label within two days of the next pulse steps aside so no numbers collide. On Plans > Month each week row is now a trace of its own: a dim phosphor baseline at the foot of the row, with a 12×8 pulse (8% fill, 2px edge) rising from it under each busy day. The next plan (1 Oct) is intensified with a bright day number. Weekday heads are two letters (Mo Tu We…) at 1.2rem, so they survive the tube's blur.

Feature 3, Figure Ground's due queue: the timetable margin, amber-edged late ticks, the dashed #6dff9c NOW line with its plate, and the dotted SOMEDAY stop are all kept. On wide screens To do uses the normal lane, so its tile and title stand where they do on every other page, and the deadlines hang in the page's own outer padding (below 79rem the lane widens again). The row's end is quieter. 'Edit, complete, or snooze' is a ghost key (transparent, 1px line-2, pencil in the label colour) that fills only on hover or open. A reminder prints only when there is one, as a bell and time in the facts column. The fold is a quiet quick-add well ('+ What needs doing…', faint on the field colour) plugged into the line, and it becomes the form's head when opened, so the head's 'Add something to do' is the one primary. On a phone the four Show keys sit in one row with their words.

Feature 4, Zenith Desk's meridian, now ends in the box. The chat box gets Home's treatment: a 1.5px brand-38% frame, E4's resting halo and E7's glow from the bottom left through masked scanlines. The axis's lit NOW plate sits on the box's top edge as its tab, so Vera's line ends in the box. On a phone the axis is the page's own spine: it drops straight from her tile with no jog, and the box widens to the spine so the NOW tab sits on its corner.

Home. The restaurants row is a neutral slate cartridge whose only colour is the restaurant kind's ring round the icon. Its eyebrow 'Something to eat' is sentence case Plex 500 14px in the label colour, and its arrow is in the label colour, so amber on Home means late or needs a look. Past LATER the dotted run lasts about 2.5rem, fades out by 6rem, and then stops, so the black beneath reads as margin. Shelf heads no longer wrap ('Lately added' stays on one line). The kind caps are painted stripes that turn down the cut corner, drawn by a pseudo-element because corner-shape split the top edge on a phone's dense screen.
Ideas: the count is the grid's section head, '12 ideas' in Instrument Sans at 1.5rem on a node with a lilac turn-in and run-on rule. The card titles became h3 beneath it.

The phone bar names every place. Memory, Family and Status fold into the Settings menu with their words (a copied base.html adds a menu group that shows only on the phone), and the menu key shows its word, so the phone's top bar is no longer bare icons.

firstDraft.name: Lit Manual
firstDraft.concept: This keeps Figure Ground's rule: every plate has a rule across the top, a figure drawn from its own data on the left and the words on the right, with a hairline between them. It changes what the judges faulted. There are no tracked caps, no paper glare, no numbering costume and no small targets. The greeting's glass pool is back, and each drawing is lit. The feel is a calm, well-set technical manual with a green tube: bone ink on green-black, blueprint on slate down the left of every page, and #6dff9c at full strength only on the short list of live things, including one live mark per figure.

name: Live Figures
tagline: The family's operator manual with its figures switched on: a round phosphor screen holding each page's one live number, figure marks that light when their row is pointed at, and every plate set on one 24px line.
concept: Figure Ground's operator manual, with its drawings made into live instruments joined to their words. Every page head holds a round phosphor tube, sunk in a slate drawing sheet inside a blueprint instrument ring, showing the page's one live figure. Every plate leads with a drawing of its own rows on graph paper ruled to the page's 24px line, and pointing at a row lights its mark, which then fades like a tube. It feels like a calm, square, well-set technical manual lit by a few small tubes, with the phosphor only where something is live and the greeting lit from the tube's side.
companions:
- Bone ink carries all the reading: #dcd8ca for text and #e8e2d0 for heads, eased to 13.45:1.
- Blueprint (#6f88b3 lines, #9fb4d6 words) is the manual's one cool companion. It draws the figures, the ring round each tube, the captions' "Fig. n.n", the chat's hung message numbers and the links.
- Slate #0f161c is the drawing sheet. Slate #20282c under a 3px paper rail (#cfcab8) means "here": the bar, the tabs, the Settings parts list, the phone tab, today on the month and the chosen company.
- Steel slips (#1b2126, a 1px #4c5760 edge and a 3px blueprint right edge) carry the family's chat lines. Vera stands on the bare page.
- Graphite #262c29 with a #3a423e lip is the bezel of every tube. Off lamps are pewter #6d7773 rings. Sage #86d9a6 is the lit edge of a pointed-at row and the ticked checkbox.
- Amber has one job, "late" and "needs a look". It is #f1af64 in words, and #ffb850 as the phosphor of the To do and Settings tubes, on neutral glass, with an amber caption lamp to match.
- Kind colours appear only as legend squares.
- #6dff9c stays on its list: the mark and its cursor, the one primary per view, the key word "plan", focus, breathing lamps, lit marks, the NOW lines, the next plan's lamp, the $2 limit tick and the tubes.
decisions: Started from r10-wild-4 as a clean sheet (variants/t1-figure-graft/sheet.css) with its own templates. I kept the manual: plates with a 2px #56615d rule, the figure column, the hairline, blueprint figures drawn from data, and chapter numbers, which now appear only in the captions ('Fig. 5.2').

FEATURE 1, the round screen (from Dessau). It is a VT323 tube with E13/E14 (three halos, .35px blur, scanlines, sheen, falloff), E12 spill and the dot-on warm-up, in a 3px graphite bezel with a lip. Round it is a blueprint ring 8px outside the glass, with a tick every 15 degrees, and a breathing power lamp at six o'clock. The figure is sized by its length in container units.
The round screen is compact (9rem, on a 168px sheet) on title-only heads and full size (12.5rem) where the head holds the page's controls (To do, Ideas) and on Home, set by a new page_head(big=...).

Round screens by page: Home shows the radar with '10:00 TOMORROW'. Chat shows her glyph screen with READY or WORKING. Ideas shows the map with 'NEAREST 18 MIN'. Plans shows 'NEXT IN 1 DAY'. To do shows amber '4 OPEN / 2 / LATE'. Status shows 'TODAY $0.00 OF $2.00' on a $0-$2.50 ring with a lit $2 limit tick. Settings shows amber 'PARTS 1 NEEDS A LOOK'. Family shows 'PEOPLE 4', Wishes 'OPEN 0' and Memory 'KEPT 0'. The form and General have no round screen.

FEATURE 2, marks keyed to rows (from Long Persistence). Every mark is drawn twice, at rest and as a phosphor copy. Rules :is(.plate,.settings-layout):has(.kN:is(:hover,:focus-within,:active)) .fig .m.kN .lit (k1 to k24), plus r1 to r24 for the radar blips, light the copy at once. The row takes a 12% steel wash and a 2px sage edge, and both fade over 1.2s. To do keys only its first 24 rows.

FEATURE 3, captions (from Night Gallery). One figcaption goes under every figure. It holds a 0.5rem lamp: lit and breathing where the figure is live, amber on an amber tube, a hollow blueprint ring otherwise. Then 'Fig. 5.2' in Plex Sans 600 #9fb4d6, then one sentence. The lamp and number hang in their own grid column, so a caption's second line starts under its first word.

FEATURE 4, the 24px line (from Phosphor Blueprint). Body is 16/24, captions 14/24, the lede 18/24, heads 28 in 48, titles and the question 48 in 48. Rows are 48 or 72; fields are 44px boxes in 48px cells. Each plate's top padding is 24px minus its rule's width, and list hairlines are drawn as outer shadows so they take no height. Every Home plate is therefore a whole number of lines (360/336/288/312/336). The graph paper (12/24/96px) lives only on the drawing sheets, anchored to the plate's first line, and the setup rungs sit on their rows.

Home: the greeting sits in an E7 pool centred on the round screen, which crosses the hairline onto the question and reaches into the page margin, with masked scanlines. 'plan' carries E1's two-layer halo. The box has 3 rows with Send as the one E3 primary, and 44px starters with 8px gaps.

Home continues: Coming up starts with the next plan. Its row is k1/r1 and has a breathing lamp hung in the margin, so the dates keep their column. Its stop on the four-week axis is lit, with a lit stretch of line from NOW. Setup and the kids' wishes sit side by side at 80rem.

Chat: a compact tube shows her glyph screen, with the glyphs set small and letter-spaced so they read as dots of light rather than columns of code. The screen is still at rest and falls only while she works. Each message's number hangs in a blueprint gutter matching the sequence diagram. Vera's lines read 'Vera · 19:48' on the bare page. The family's lines are steel slips on the right, with 'Sam · 19:47' on the slip's own line and a slate initial square after it. The date appears once, as a divider.

Plans month: the month spans the page, and its key comes back as Fig. 4.2 under the table: hatched, shaded and lit-lamp swatches, each named in one sentence. Today is the slate cell with the paper rail and an E20 lamp.
Status: under the title sits a register line, 'OpenAI answers · 3 of 9 lamps lit'. The wiring leads plate 2, and each lamp row lights its port.
Settings: the exploded machine leads 'The parts', and each row lights its callout. On General the machine sits over the parts list with the current callout lit.

Phone: each round screen shrinks beside its title. On Home a 5.5rem radar sits beside Vera's line and the date, and the question runs the full width on one line at 2.5rem. Every other figure folds to a 44px strip in the Tab order.
Every page has 0 targets under 44px. Sentence case is used on every control, Plex Mono only for figures, VT323 only on glass, and dates in words (To do, and now the idea page's 'added 27 Sep').

Pointing at a row lights its mark wherever there is one: stops, blips on the round radar, tally squares, arrows, ports, callouts, rungs, kind bars and days. The steel-and-sage afterglow is visible at 120 and 380ms in the motion capture.

Her glyph screen is still a field of glyphs. Set small, spaced and still at rest, it reads as dots, but a family member who saw the Matrix before may still see it.
On compact tubes a long small word ('NEEDS A LOOK') steps down to 15px so it stays inside the round glass. Top words stay at 1.05rem.

name: Flight Console, Go
tagline: The family's weeks flown from a calm console, each thing said once: a readout rail of figures heads every page, the flight plan says when with stops numbered to the rows, and the phosphor lights only what is live.
concept: This is Flight Console with its costume taken off and its promise kept: each thing is said once. The readout rail heads every page and gives figures that the page does not say anywhere else, as 56px links. The flight plan says when, in the same drawing on Home and on Plans: a lit NOW needle, Next up as a lit square, later stops as violet rings numbered to the rows, and each leg's length over its arc. The rows say what. On Status the annunciator windows are the rows' own column. firstDraft.name: Lamps and Ladders
firstDraft.concept: The 1969 flight console, finished rather than costumed. The phosphor's glowing dots on the black return as instruments that each do a job: a jewelled pilot lamp for anything on, a T-minus lamp ladder beside every hop, and a moving-coil needle that reads the day's spend. Everything else is matte slate, steel and Plex type, so the page feels calm and exact, and your eye goes straight to what is lit.

name: Switchboard, Trued
tagline: Home is the map of the whole service, every page a line of the contents with its lamp and its count, the terminal among them as page 200 with the question typed on its glass; every other page opens on one module (plate, primary, tools, green screen) beside a register of the same one-line rows.
concept: This is the videotex sommaire with its faults trued. Home is still the map of every page. Each cell is sized to what it holds and headed by one contents line: lamp, number, name, leader and count. The lit terminal and Status run down the left, and setup, Plans and To do run down the right. Every inner page opens on the same rack: one graphite module holding the plate (with the page's figure), the one green primary, one bank of latched keys and the page's own green screen. Beside it sits a register of 44px contents rows whose dotted leaders run from each name to its facts. It should feel like a calm, square panel in bone and slate, where light comes only from the machine: the tubes, her screen, the mark and caret, Send, the well being typed in, focus, and the lamps that are on.
companions:
- **Bone #cdc6b5** (the accent, C≈0.02) replaces brass. It carries the household pages (Home, Vera, Memory, Family, Status, Settings): their 2px caps, icons and counts, the row-zero words, the month's name, Status's figures and the typed words in the well.
- **Steel** means "here" wherever it appears: the current key in row zero and in the phone's Fastext row, latched filter keys, today's leaf on the month, and the current settings page. It is a #56697b fill with a #a9c4d8 top edge; I darkened it from #5f7689 so bone ink on it passes 4.5:1. A 12% steel wash is also the row afterglow, the family's chat bubbles have a 3px #93b4c8 edge, and a 7px steel dot means waiting. A 10% steel tint marks the weekend columns and their heads on the month.
- **Pewter #8794a2** is the "off" ring.
- **Clay #a99389** (OKLCH 0.68 0.03 46) is new in this revision. It is the restaurants' own colour (their kind word, fork icon and key), a grounded earth 16 dE or more from amber, coral, olive and bone, so that amber has one job.
- **Amber #eaa76b** is state only: late and needs-a-look. It appears as bars, rings, the setup cap and words ("was due 3 days ago", "2 late" on the To do plate as a link to the late list, "1 needs a look").
- **Section colours** appear only as a 2px cap, an icon and a figure: lilac for Ideas ("12 saved"), sky for Plans ("2 to come", "in 4 days"), teal for To do ("4 open") and pink for Wishes.
- **Kinds** keep their low-chroma hues on icons and kind words.
- **Green #6dff9c** stays exact, as does the screen green.
decisions: Started from r12-wmut-1 as the brief asked. The sheet is assembled from parts (variants/t1-switchboard-refine/tools/parts, built by tools/build.sh) into a 145K clean sheet within the 200K budget. I kept the parent's green screens, radar, her screen, controls, sign-in and lost pages. Row zero, the rack, the rows, the lamps, Home and every register are rebuilt.

One nav. The six places are in row zero, each with its icon in its section colour and its word in bone, as 44px keys, then a hairline divider, then Memory, Family, Status and Settings in words. The current key is a steel cell with a #a9c4d8 top edge, a 5px #6dff9c LED and its page number in 12px mono; no other key shows a number. The second key row, P100·SOMMAIRE and the P-tiles are gone. On the phone the places are the Fastext foot row (now fully opaque) and the tools are icons with labels for screen readers.

Home: the machine is laid out apart from the family's things (round-12 principle a). Down the left are the terminal and 900 Status (lamps plus the lamp key). Down the right are Finish setting up (first and widest, amber cap, '3 left', numbered 44px steps), then 400 Plans ('4 more', 'After Next up', dates set on the digit, 'in 4 days' in sky Plex Sans), then 500 To do ('4 · 2 late', Who/Due heads, amber-ringed ticks, 'was due 3 days ago' in amber words). Below them come 300 Ideas, then Wishes, Memory and Family as short cells, and 990 Settings as a three-column mini sommaire with 998 and its amber bar first. Both columns end together, and Home is 1730px tall.

The terminal is page 200. The case's top line is her contents line. The glass is sized to its content: NEXT UP with a breathing lamp, the plan's name at the 2rem tube step, when, [TOMORROW], '> 4 more on the radar' (to #coming), and the radar. Then comes a dashed rule and the question at 2.9rem, the largest thing on the glass and on Home, with 'plan' as the one white-hot word and a Plex Mono apostrophe. The well is #07110b glass with a VT323 '>' and a block cursor, the family's words in Plex 17px bone, a lit caret and E4 focus. The deck holds From, 'Send where I am', the mic and the one E3 Send. Under it the three ways to start are sunk-number keys, and E7's scanlined pool spills from the case's lower left.

One row drawing, now with a true leader: the name and its dots are one cell (.what > .t + .dots), so the dotted leader starts where each name ends and runs to the facts. It sits on the text's baseline and is capped at 46rem. The name column is minmax(0,1fr) everywhere and the separate dots column is gone (Home Plans, To do, Ideas, Wishes; the Ideas, To do, Plans list, Settings, Family and Restaurants registers). Hover and focus light a row at once with a 12% steel wash and a 2px edge, fading over 1.2s, which is still visible in all four motion-glow frames.

Figures have one face. A count is condensed Plex Sans 500 with tabular figures in its section's colour: 32px on the plate, 24px on a cell head, 22px on Status's lamp cells. Plex Mono is kept for times, dates, drive times, compass points and page numbers set in columns. Relative phrases ('in 4 days', 'was due 3 days ago') are Plex Sans words with tabular figures.

The inner pages' plate now states the page's figure beside the title on a shared last baseline: Ideas '12 saved', To do '4 open' over '2 late' (amber, a 44px link to ?when=late), Plans '2 to come', Status '$1.26 in 30 days · 6 calls', Family 'N people', Restaurants 'N to try'. The module's padding is tighter (0.8rem) and the screens' bezels are thinner (0.35rem sides). To do's module now ends at about y=860 on a 900px screen, so it stays sticky without the tall class.

On a phone the rack reorders: plate and tools, then the register, then the green screen, so the list is on the first screen rather than under the tube. The module's pieces keep their cap and seams, and there is no sideways scroll.

Four signals with a key (L260): on is a breathing lit disc, only the first in a list breathes; waiting is a steel dot; off is a pewter ring; needs-a-look or late is an amber bar. Red appears only when something has stopped.

Light is kept to the phosphor list: E1 on 'plan', E2 on the mark and caret, E3 on Send and the primaries, E4 on the well and fields, E5 on focus including selects, E6 as the top haze under an 88% bar, E7 and E12 on the case, E8 on cells, E10 on #coming, #todo-list and now the To do add form, E12-E17 on every tube at screenGlow 1.0, and E19-E21. Nothing else glows. Cells come up in reading order 50ms apart, and all motion stops under reduced motion. The MC block keeps .crt-tube > :not(.radar){filter:none}.
title: What’s the *plan*? It is kept from the draft, as the studio critic asked. It names FamilyDB's job, since every part of the planner (weekends, ideas to keep, the calendar, reminders, wishes) is a plan being made, and it reads as an invitation to tell Vera one. It fits one line on a phone at 2.4rem and on desktop at 2.9rem, where it is now the largest thing on the glass. It is still the box's label. 'plan' is the one lit word, echoing the Plans page and her 'Next up'.
measures:
- **Contrast:** ink_on_bg 15.15:1, brand_on_bg 15.28:1. brand, screen and halo are exact #6dff9c, and glow, screenGlow and topGlow are all 1.0.
- **Green share of colour:** Home 61.1%, Ideas 57.8%, Chat 71.5%, Status 64.9%.
- **Hue entropy:** Home 0.522, Ideas 0.451, Chat 0.409, Status 0.361.
- **Bright green per mille:** Home 4.23, Ideas 11.0, Chat 3.95, Status 1.48.
- **Colour distance (CIEDE2000):** kinds 17.6 typical, 6.2 deutan, 7.6 protan; sections 17.6, 7.9, 7.9. The check still measures restaurant as `people`; the page now draws it in clay, measured separately at 16 dE or more from every neighbour.
- **Small targets:** 0 under 44px on Home, and 0 on every rendered page (home, home-phone, ideas, todo, chat, chat-phone, plans, status, settings, form, general, login, lost). Two found during revision were fixed: the Next up title link and the '2 late' link.
- **Other checks:** no sideways scroll anywhere; I also fixed a 1px phone overflow on inner pages from the module cap under display:contents. Smallest text is 12px.
- **Flagged:** one WARN, the page's words differ by 32.2% on home-phone, from the sommaire's contents lines.
- **Result:** 0 hard failures.
strengths: Home is a real contents page of the service. Each cell is headed by one line (lamp, number, name, a leader that now runs from the name to its count, and the count), and each is sized to what it holds. The terminal is page 200 among them, and setup ranks first and widest.

The leader finally works as a typographic device. On every register the dots start at the end of each name and stop at its facts, on the baseline and capped at 46rem. The full-width Settings head runs its leader to '9 · 1 needs a look' at the right edge.

A clear terminal hierarchy: 'What’s the plan?' at 2.9rem is Home's largest head, with 'plan' white-hot, above the 2rem plan name. The question is typed over a Plex well with a lit caret, a VT323 prompt and a blinking block, and the case spills its lit pool from below.

A coherent figure system: every list page states its figure beside its title, in its section colour, on a shared baseline, with a mono legend over a note. To do's '2 late' is amber words and a link to the late list. Counts are condensed sans figures everywhere; mono is only for times, dates, drives and page numbers.

Green screens now say what their pages do not. Plans leads with the weekend, names weeks by their Monday ('28 Sep') and folds the weeks gone into one dim line. To do's tube is dated for its late/this-week buckets and names the next thing due. Status's tube keeps today against the limit while the plate carries the 30-day cost. Settings' glass wraps rather than clips.
Amber has one job at last: clay takes the restaurants, steel is 'here', and pewter is 'off', each with a single meaning, with a legend on Home and in Status.

Careful setting in the facts columns: drive times close up their hours ('2h 10 min') and right-align on the minutes, with the compass point in its own 2ch column. Dates are set on the digit ('Sun  4 Oct'). Relative phrases are sans words with tabular figures.
No target under 44px on any page, one nav, sentence-case controls, and a phone rack that puts each page's list before its summary screen.
weaknesses: On Ideas the radar screen still starts at about y=740 on a 900px screen, with only its top on the first screen. Search, a five-row kind bank and the More filters fold come first, which the judges asked for. I could not shorten them further without breaking 44px keys.

Status's three lamp cells now stretch to a shared bottom, as the critic asked, so Who answers and Keys carry 70-110px of empty graphite at their foot. On Home the right-hand To do cell likewise ends with about 60px of darkspace so that the two columns meet.
The Plans screen draws only the month grid's own weeks (the view gives the template nothing further out). In the month's last week it is thin: the weekend line, 'Earlier · no plans' and one bar.
The Settings glass breaks 'gpt-6-/luna' at its hyphen now that lines wrap instead of clipping.

When To do's add form is open there are two green buttons in view: the plate's 'Add something to do' and the form's 'Save task'. The form opens by :target, so a second press of the plate's key only scrolls to it.
Page numbers (200, 300, 990…) remain as quiet 12px mono in row zero, on plates and on the map. They are the lineage's identity, but a skeptic may still call them costume the family never uses.
Home's Memory cell still says one line and a link, because the Home view passes no memory count to fill it with.
The words differ from today by 32% on Home because the sommaire names each page's contents.

Next up's name spans the glass on one line, the radar sits beside when-and-more (rows 3-5), and '> 4 more on the radar' is set at the small tube step so it no longer breaks.

The leader now runs from the name to its fact. crit: Broken on phone Home. The first way to start ('1 What should we do this weekend?') is drawn as a tall empty box of about 100px with its words at the foot (home-phone shot). The desktop rule `.minitel .starters li:first-child { flex-basis: 100% }` (sheet.css 1178) outranks the phone's `.minitel .starters li { flex: none }`, and in the phone's column flex a 100% basis becomes a height. firstDraft.name: Switchboard, Trued
firstDraft.concept: This is the videotex sommaire with its fixable faults trued. Home is still the map of every page, but the cells are now sized to what they hold and headed by one contents line (lamp, number, name, leader, count). The machine and the family's things are laid out apart: the lit terminal and Status run down the left, and setup, Plans and To do run down the right. Every inner page opens the same rack: one graphite module (plate, the one green primary, one bank of latched keys, and the page's own green screen) beside a register of the same 44px contents rows. It should feel like a calm, square, bone-and-slate panel where light comes only from the machine: the tubes, her screen, the mark and caret, Send, the well being typed in, focus and the lamps that are on.

name: Switchboard, Lamp-lit
tagline: The family's videotex service as a switchboard: Home is the map of every page, each cell's picture a mosaic counted from its own data and hung beside what it counts, every tube set as a terminal's lines, and only what is live gives off the phosphor's light.
concept: Home is still the service's sommaire: a rack of graphite cells, each headed by its numbered contents line. Each picture now hangs at its cell's top right, beside what it counts: the next four weeks as a calendar with the weekend set apart, the to-dos as a clipboard of bars, the ideas as a bulb, the wishes as a gift, the family as figures a head apart. The terminal types the question in double-height lines on the glass, over a Plex well for the family's own words. It should feel like a calm, matte panel of bone and graphite where light only means something is live: the tube, "plan", Send, a lit lamp, one breathing block, the LED on the key you are on.
companions: Bone (#cdc6b5) is the house accent in place of the parent's brass. It carries the key-row words, block figures and the bulb's base, the matte "set" lamp (a 0.55rem square at 72%, no halo), today's ring in the calendar, and links on Home, Status and Settings. Steel (#536979) has one job, "here" and "chosen", and now draws it one way everywhere with bone ink and a lit 5px LED: the current key, latched keys, the settings list's current part, the menu's current item, the Settings key in row zero, the phone's current top-bar icon, the pointed row in every choice list, the family's chat bubbles, and today's leaf on the month. Pewter (#5d676e) draws the "not set up" rings and the rules between lamp banks. Amber (#eaa76b) has one job, late or needs a look: "was due" words, amber-ringed ticks, the lamp bar, the setup cap and To do's late count on the glass. The section colours (lilac, sky, teal, pink, olive, coral) appear only as 2px caps on Home cells, icons, kind words, and matte mosaic blocks. #6dff9c stays on the mark and caret, Send and the primaries, "plan", the tubes, lit lamps, at most one live block per picture, LEDs, focus, and the picked-choice block.
decisions: Figures hang, they are no longer pinned to a foot. figure_mosaic() takes a pitch (Home 10px, so 8px blocks and 2px gaps; plates 9px) and a split column, which opens a 3px gutter. Each Home picture floats at its cell's top right under the contents line. Its fact is said beside it, and the cell's own rows run beside and under it. A register (Plans, To do) clears the figure so its facts columns stay whole; short lists (Ideas, Wishes' kids) run around it. Every cell now ends on its own rows, and Home fell from 1672px to about 1590px.

Figures read by shape, not tint. The calendar has week rows with the weekend set off by a gutter (the 30%/45% tint is gone), and today is ringed in bone, or lit when a plan is on it. The clipboard has a bone clip and a bar per open task (amber late, teal due, dim undated, lit only when due today). The bulb has a block per idea: the newest in kind colours, one breathing while it waits, a bone base. The gift has a bone bow and a lid that turns amber while a wish waits. The family is figures of head, gap and body (grown-ups 3 blocks tall, kids 2) drawn from the kid list. The Ideas plate uses the same bulb, and the form's plate an empty one with the new idea in it. Memory has no figure until something is kept.

Captions state the fact: '5 plans in the next four weeks / 1 weekend still free', '2 late, 1 due on a day, 1 kept for no day' (with '2 late' a 44px link to To do), '12 ideas kept', 'Sam, Alex, Maya and Theo / 2 grown-ups, 2 kids'.

Each Home add key moves up under its fact, beside the picture, as the inner pages put their one action on the plate. This evens out row 3 (To do, Ideas, Vera plus Memory now end together) and leaves the rows as the cell's last content.

Lamps are a five-state code: lit for live, a matte bone square for set, a pewter ring for not set up, an amber bar for needs a look, red only when stopped. Settings (its well and tally) and Home's 990 cell use 'set', so the largest cluster of green outside the terminal is gone. Home's 990 keeps only the tally '8 set · 1 needs a look' and the amber row '998 Sign-in and security'. Home's 900 keeps its three lamps with two-line legends that state each lamp (Telegram / not set up), with '1 on · 2 off' as its contents count, which the phone's folded row still shows. The repeated word list is gone.

One label voice. Labels, legends, column heads, captions, tags, month heads and chat stamps are all Plex Sans 600 at 13px, untracked, sentence case, in label ink. The later rules that won the cascade (register heads, bank labels, crumbs) were fixed in place. Capitals stay only for the inverse legends on the glass. Chat stamps now read 'Sam · Sun 27 Sep, 19:47': a stamp macro works out the weekday from the view's '27 Sep, 19:47', and the family's name leads on the right side too. Role and status tags are capitalised (Admin, Parent, Kid).

Ideas' Kind is a numbered choice list, as For and Status are: 01 Any kind to 08 Seasonal, each with its mosaic icon in its kind's colour, the chosen one marked by the lit block. Kind and For pair on one row; Status gets the full width so 'any but dropped' never wraps. The module shrinks by about 250px, and the radar's scope is now on the first screen. One kind-colour map (--k) replaces the three copies the sheet had.

On the phone, each inner page's module comes apart so the list follows the plate and its controls. The order is plate, then search and filters (or the lamp well), then the register, then the screen and the rest. Every board child has an order, so Status's extra modules stay last. Ideas' first row moves from about 1200px down to about 640px, and To do's from about 870px to about 530px. On the phone's To do, Edit moves to the second line beside Who, clear of the title.
Home To do: Who is 5rem and Due 9.75rem, so 'due tomorrow, 19:56' fits. Titles wrap to two balanced lines instead of an ellipsis. The column heads get a hairline under them.
The title's apostrophe is the straight ASCII one. VT323's curly apostrophe is the tall tick the judges have flagged for three rounds; the straight one reads as a typewriter's.

Wishes' kid lines sit on their lists: .cell.half.kid-line gets min-height 0. The form's plate gets '300 Ideas /' and the bulb. Memory's screen lights only when something is kept, so no glass is lit empty. On the phone the Settings sommaire's second lines wrap instead of cutting off, and the Plans list's 'How soon' head is label ink, not link blue.
title: What's the *plan*? It is the family's own phrase and an invitation to tell Vera something, not to be asked. "Plan" is the planner's whole job in one lit word: the weekend, an outing, a reminder, the calendar. It also stops repeating the inverse NEXT UP legend four rows above it on the same glass, as the draft's "What comes *next*?" did. At 16 cells it stays one double-height line on a 390px phone, and its straight apostrophe avoids VT323's tall-tick curly quote.
measures: Final full render: 0 hard checks failed. The one guideline missed is words: Home differs from today by 32.4%, from the sommaire and the stated facts. ink_on_bg 15.15, brand_on_bg 15.28. glow, screenGlow and topGlow are all 1.0, and brand and screen are exactly #6dff9c. Green share of colour: Home 50.6%, Ideas 53.0%, Chat 47.7%, Status 36.5%. Hue entropy: 0.60, 0.57, 0.57, 0.61. Bright green on Home is 4.5 per mille. Small targets: 0 of 69 under 44px on Home, and 0 on every one of the 13 rendered pages (home-phone 0/64, To do 0/101). No sideways scroll on any page, and the smallest text is 12px. removed.txt is empty. The clean sheet is 176,099 of 200,000 characters.
strengths: The pictures are now page content, not corner ornaments. Each hangs beside the rows it counts, reads by its shape (a calendar with a weekend gutter, a clipboard, a bulb, a gift, people a head apart) and carries its fact in words. Only one block per picture can light, and only when something is live.

Glare is back on the phosphor list alone: the tube, 'plan' with its hot core over the bloom, Send, lit lamps and LEDs. Settings' nine parts are matte bone squares and the amber bar, so a part that is only set no longer glows.

One grammar holds on every page. 'Here' is the steel reverse cell with a lit LED, in the key row, row zero's Settings key, the phone's top bar, the settings list, the menu and every choice list. Every label is one sentence-case voice. Every dropdown is the numbered videotex list, and Ideas' Kind now joins them with its icons in their colours.
It is usable on the phone: the list comes straight after the plate and its tools on every inner page, To do's Edit no longer collides with titles, and there are 0 small targets on 13 pages.

Home's rows balance. Row 3's three columns end together because the add keys sit in the figure bands. The Status and Settings cells lost their repeated lamp words and well, and Family's names sit beside its figures.
weaknesses: Home's view passes only the newest four ideas, so the bulb and its 'waiting to be looked up' fact can only count those four. In the demo the two waiting ideas are older, so Home's bulb never lights and the fact reads only '12 ideas kept'. The Ideas plate, which has every row, does light its block.
Row 4 still has 30-60px of slack in Settings and Status beside Wishes. Home's Memory cell has about 40px between its head and its one key, because the view passes no count to fill it.

Tab order on the phone: the module comes apart by CSS order, so the Ideas radar's two links, 'Save a thought for later' and Settings' Setup link come before the list in Tab order while they appear after it. Desktop Tab order is unchanged and matches the drawing.
The plate pictures at a 9px pitch are 43-64px: the bulb and the gift are narrow by shape. They are below the 70-90px asked for on Home's cells.

Family and Wishes keep their green screens (Family's '4 people'), which the lineage brief said to drop on pages with nothing live. I kept them because the critic named Family's double-height figure as working, and dropped only Memory's empty one.

Status's own well still lights six lamps, because there 'on' means working now. The Settings page's well is matte, but it is still a dark recessed box holding nine small squares, which some may find a heavy frame for so little.
revisions: Mosaics: pitch and split arguments; figures hung at each cell's top right beside their rows (a float, with registers clearing it); shapes in place of tints (weekend gutter, head-gap-body people, a clip, a bulb); captions that state facts; the Ideas plate uses Home's bulb; Memory's figure appears only with data.

Glare: a matte .light.set for set parts on the Settings page and in Home's tally. Home 990 lost its well and keeps the tally plus the amber row. Home 900 lost .lamp-words, its legends carry state on a second line, and its count is '1 on · 2 off'.

Phone: .board > .side comes apart with display: contents, ordered plate, controls, register, then the rest; Status's spend and lamps come early. To do's Edit moves to the second line with a tighter title line, and the Settings sommaire's states wrap.
Ideas: Kind is a base-select numbered list with kind icons, paired with For; Status is full width; the latched kind bank and its CSS are gone.
Title: 'What's the *plan*?' as the critic proposed, with a straight apostrophe.

Sentence case: one label rule, plus fixes to the later cascade rules for .register li.reg-head, .keybank legend, .bank-label and .crumbs. Tags are included, and role and status tags capitalised. Chat stamps are 'Sam · Sun 27 Sep, 19:47', name first on both sides.
'Here': .settings-nav and .menu-list current items, the Settings summary (.menu.here) and the phone's .tools current icon are all steel reverse with a lit LED.

Wishes kid lines min-height 0. The form's plate has '300' and the bulb. Home To do's Due column is 9.75rem, Who 5rem, and titles wrap balanced. Add keys sit under each fact. Family's names go into its caption. Memory's empty screen is removed. Forced-colours handling added for the set lamp.

Declined: the form's Kind as a select. Its own template says a kind is 'a list, not a closed choice: the model invents a kind when none fits, and so may you'. A closed list would take that choice from the family, so it stays a text box with suggestions.

Declined: a colour cap on the form's plate. No plate carries one: by the lineage's rule 2px caps sit on Home cells only, so the form now matches every other plate (number and figure) rather than gaining a cap the others lack.

Declined, in part: the critic asked Status's tally to be the only count. I tried a big tally under Home's strip, found it repeated the count and left the phone's folded row saying only '3', and went back to the count in the contents line with no second tally.
crit: The mosaics are corner ornaments, not page content. They are 38-54px thumbnails pinned to each cell's lower-right foot (.cell-fig { margin-top: auto }, 6px blocks on the fixed 8px pitch in figure_mosaic() in _ui.html). That is the 'wash in the corner or a few icons' the owner turned down. The shared foot line also leaves 80-100px of empty darkspace in To do, Wishes and Family. Fixes: give figure_mosaic a pitch argument (Home 10px, i.e. 8px blocks with 2px gaps; plates 9px) so each picture is 70-90px. Set it at the top right beside the cell's rows, not on a foot, so each cell ends with its own content. Make each figure read by shape rather than transparency: Plans' 28 days in week rows with an extra 3px gutter before the Sat and Sun columns, instead of 30% vs 45% blocks. Family's figures get a head block, a gap, then a body (adults 3 tall, kids 2), so they stop reading as a barcode. The Ideas plate uses the same bulb as Home instead of the 6x2 swatch strip. Drop Memory's plate figure (six empty blocks) until the view passes a count. Captions state the fact, not the key: '12 ideas · 2 waiting to be looked up', not 'the newest 4 in their colours'.

Glare guard broken on Settings (Home's 990 cell and the Settings plate). The well lights eight #6dff9c lamps with 6px and 16px halos for parts that are only 'set'. That is the largest cluster of light outside the terminal, and 'set' is not live. Add a matte state, .light.set (a 0.55rem bone #cdc6b5 square at about 70%, no box-shadow), and use it for set parts and the '8 set' tally glyph; keep the amber bar for needs a look. On Home, take the well out of 990 and leave the tally plus the one amber row '998 Sign-in and security'. On Home's 900 Status cell, remove the .lamp-words list, which repeats the three lamp legends, and put the state in each legend ('Telegram · off'). Both cells lose about 70px, which also closes row 4's empty space under Wishes and Family.

On the phone (max-width 640px), the whole module (plate, filters, tube) comes before the register on every inner page. The first row of the list lands about 1200px down on Ideas, 870px on To do, 830px on Settings and 700px on Plans. In the 640px query, set .board > .side { display: contents } and order the page as .side > .plate, then .main, then the filters and the .screen-cell. Or fold the filters into a single 'Filter · any kind' <details> key under the plate. The list is what someone opened the page for, so it should come right after the plate's primary.

Ideas on desktop: the 10-key Kind bank (.keybank, five rows of 50px) pushes the radar tube below the fold and makes the module three times as tall as its plate. Make Kind a numbered choice list like the Status and For selects beside it (the grafted base-select: '01 Any', '02 Activity' and so on, each with its kind icon in its colour). That brings the radar tube up beside the register's first rows. The same select should replace the form's Kind field (/ideas/new), which is a plain text box today.

The greeting's title (_ask.html h1.ask-question, 'What comes next?'). The lit word repeats the inverse NEXT UP legend four rows above it on the same glass. The question also reads as asking Vera what comes next, when the box is for telling her. Proposal: 'What’s the plan?'. It is the family's own phrase and an invitation to tell her something, it names the planner's job in one lit word, and at 16 cells it stays one double-height line on a 390px phone. If 'next' is kept, rename the legend to 'Coming up'.

Tracked mono capitals are left over from the parent, and the lineage's own fix was sentence case. They sit in the sheet.css L1909 group and in every rule that sets text-transform: uppercase on label, legend, table.data th and caption, .reg-heads, .register li.reg-head, .said-by, .waiting-cell h3, .keybank > legend, table.month th and .changed. On the pages that means: the Family role chips ADMIN/PARENT/KID, Wishes' 'IN 86 DAYS', Status' '10 LOOKED UP', 'EVERY LINE AT A GLANCE' and 'BY KIND OF CALL', the chat's '27 SEP, 19:47 SAM', and 'FROM' on the deck. Set them in sentence case, Plex Sans 600 at 0.8125rem, tracking 0, in label ink #a9b4af. Keep capitals only for the inverse legends on the glass (.crt .inverse). Chat stamps become 'Sam · Sun 27 Sep, 19:47'.

'Here' still has three looks. .settings-nav a[aria-current] (L1587) and .menu-list a[aria-current] (L253) mark it with a bone-tinted cell and a bone inset bar. Draw them like the key row and the latched keys: a steel #536979 reverse cell, bone ink and the lit 5px LED in the top right. Two more places where the lineage is not carried through: on Wishes, .cell.half.kid-line puts one contents line in a 128px band, so give it min-height: 0 and let the Maya and Theo heads sit on their three lists. The form's plate (/ideas/new) has no '300', no bulb and no cap, so give it the Ideas plate's number, figure and cap like every other plate.

Crowded rows. Home's 500 To do cuts 'Book the campsite at Silver F…' because of the fixed 5rem Who and 10rem Due tracks (.reg-heads and its row grid, 2.75rem 1fr 5rem 10rem). Take Due to 8.5rem and let titles wrap to two balanced lines instead of an ellipsis. On the phone's To do, 'Book the campsite at Silver Falls' runs into 'Edit' with no gap: put Edit on the second line beside Who, or give the title column a 0.75rem gutter.
